in_arabic.name: أنباس
in_arabic.meaning: أنباس هو اسم يعني الشخص الذي يأتي بالخير الكثير
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أنباس هو من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني الخير والنماء، وقد ورد في بعض الروايات أنه اسم من أسماء الله الحسنى، ويعني الشخص الذي يأتي بالخير الكثير للناس، ويتصف بالكرم والجود. وقد ذكر بعض العلماء أن هذا الاسم مشتق من الفعل 'أنبس' الذي يعني الانبساط والفرح، وقد كان يستخدم في العصر الجاهلي كاسم للشخص الذي يأتي بالبشارة والخير.

in_urdu.name: انباس
in_urdu.meaning: انباس کا مطلب ہے خیر کی فراوانی لانے والا شخص
in_urdu.long_meaning: انباس ایک ایسا نام ہے جو خیر اور کثرت کے مفہوم کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، اور یہ بعض روایات میں الله کے ہی ناموں میں سے ایک ہے۔ یہ نام کرم اور سخاوت کی خصوصیات والے شخص کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے، جو لوگوں کے لئے بہت سا خیر لاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अनबास
in_hindi.meaning: अनबास का अर्थ है बहुतायत में अच्छाई लाने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: अनबास नाम की उत्पत्ति संस्कृत और अरबी भाषाओं से हुई है, और इसका अर्थ है बहुतायत में अच्छाई लाने वाला। यह नाम उन व्यक्तियों के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो दूसरों के लिए बहुत सारी खुशियाँ और समृद्धि लाते हैं।

data.cultural_impact: The name Anbas carries a strong cultural impact as it embodies the spirit of bravery, courage, and strength. In various Islamic societies, the name Anbas is given to boys as a symbol of their strength and their potential to be powerful and influential leaders, akin to a mighty lion that fearlessly leads its pride.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Anbas holds deep significance as it is a reminder of the courage and resilience required to follow the path ofrighteousness and self-improvement. Just as a lion fearlessly faces and overcomes its challenges, a person named Anbas is encouraged to face and overcome his or her personal struggles and temptations with bravery and determination, drawing strength from the name's spiritual meaning and the legacy of the noble companion after whom it is named. Furthermore, the name Anbas is a reminder of the Islamic belief in the power of Allah and the importance of standing up for truth and justice, even in the face of adversity.

historical_references.reference: Anbas ibn Al- Ashath was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad and took part in many battles including Khaybar and Hunayn. He was also known for his generosity and hospitality. Anbas became the governor of Kufa, Iraq, in 632 AD and established the first mosque there.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, establishment of the first mosque in Kufa, Iraq.

historical_references.reference: Anbas al-Sawi, a famous Sufi saint and scholar from Basra, Iraq, is believed to have lived during the 9th century AD. He is known for his piety, asceticism, and teaching of Islamic mysticism. Anbas al-Sawi is still revered in Iraq and has numerous shrines dedicated to him.
